contracts.name: Browser → Gateway REST
contracts.rule: Frontend normally calls Gateway, not internal services.

contracts.name: Service outbound RPC
contracts.rule: Reuse the bounded multiplexed process transport: one robust connection, channel, exchange and callback queue per outbound client; route replies and streams by unique hop correlation IDs, clean waiter state on every terminal path, and preserve signed identity plus request/trace context.

contracts.name: RAG downstream calls
contracts.rule: Extend the existing backend client for RAG downstream operations and use the shared multiplexed transport; streaming shares its bounded callback resource and routes ordered events by hop correlation ID.

contracts.name: Durable ingestion pipeline
contracts.rule: Files publishes typed passage work on embedding.jobs.requested; Embedding publishes typed vector work on vector_db.upsert.requested. The embedding.requests topic is extraction-only until document parsing moves out of Embedding. Critical flow targets at-least-once + idempotency.

contracts.name: RAG eval persistence
contracts.rule: Benchmark extensions reuse current eval dataset/run store.

contracts.name: Service liveness and readiness
contracts.rule: /live is process-only and normally returns 200; /ready returns 503 whenever a dependency required for the service's primary workload is unavailable, while optional degraded dependencies do not gate readiness.

contracts.name: Memory Agent policy to canonical Memory V2 service
contracts.rule: The model receives bounded conversation and tenant/user-scoped candidates, cannot choose scope or reference other IDs, and never persists directly. The complete plan must pass schema and deterministic business validation; background delete is unauthorized and any unvalidated/failing plan degrades to no mutation.

contracts.name: Durable deletion identity across MongoDB and Qdrant
contracts.transport: MongoDB collection scoped by tenant and owner user
contracts.rule: The deletion identity is written first and is never deleted by reconciliation. It carries only memory_id, owner, memory_class, content_hash, fact_key, preference_key, scope_key, deleted_at, provenance and revision — no memory text — and is scoped like every other memory row, so one tenant's or user's deletion never suppresses another's fact. A canonical row that carries a deletion identity is finished as a delete by reconciliation and never re-embedded; a replayed delete reports the same deleted outcome instead of not-found, and an unknown id is still not-found.
